# Test-ZbxAgentItem

## SYNOPSIS

Answers an item key the way an agent session would, without a server.

## SYNTAX

### Answer (Default)

```
Test-ZbxAgentItem [-Key] <ZabbixItemKey> [-HostName <string>] [-Session <string>] [-Timeout <TimeSpan>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Raw

```
Test-ZbxAgentItem [-Key] <ZabbixItemKey> [-HostName <string>] [-Session <string>] [-Timeout <TimeSpan>] -Raw [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

Writes one ZabbixAgentAnswer per key (or, with -Raw, just its value or error text), and no error: a key no handler supports is an answer whose Error is "This agent does not answer the key.", as the agent itself would answer. A key that does not parse is refused by the binder (-Key is a ZabbixItemKey); a -Session that is not running ends the command (ZabbixAgentNotFound).

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Answer a built-in key locally

```powershell
Test-ZbxAgentItem -Key 'agent.version'
Test-ZbxAgentItem -Key 'vfs.fs.size[/,pfree]' -Raw
```

No session, no network: the built-in keys answer agent.ping, agent.version, agent.hostname and system.uname, and the bundled items answer Zabbix's own keys, measured on this computer.

### Example 2: Get the bare value with -Raw

```powershell
Test-ZbxAgentItem -Key 'agent.hostname' -Hostname 'web-01' -Raw
```

-Raw writes the answer's value (or its error text) instead of the whole answer; -Hostname sets what agent.hostname answers (the computer name by default).

### Example 3: Test a running session's own handlers

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Port 30150
Register-ZbxPassiveAgentHandler -Name 'web-agent' -Key 'app.health' -ScriptBlock { 'ok' }
Test-ZbxAgentItem -Key 'app.health' -Session 'web-agent' | Select-Object Key, Value, IsSupported, Error
Test-ZbxAgentItem -Key 'no.such.key' -Session 'web-agent' | Select-Object Key, Value, IsSupported, Error
Stop-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

-Session dispatches through that session's full handler set, its scriptblocks and plugins included, exactly as a server's check would. A key nothing answers comes back with Error set rather than as a terminating error.

### Example 4: Build a key of your own from bundled ones

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Port 30150
Register-ZbxPassiveAgentHandler -Name 'web-agent' -Key 'app.disk.alarm' -ScriptBlock {
    if ([double](Test-ZbxAgentItem -Key 'vfs.fs.size[/,pused]' -Raw) -gt 90) { 1 } else { 0 }
}
Test-ZbxAgentItem -Key 'app.disk.alarm' -Session 'web-agent' -Raw
Stop-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

A scriptblock handler reads bundled keys with Test-ZbxAgentItem -Raw: here app.disk.alarm answers 1 when the root file system is more than 90 percent full.

### Example 5: Test several keys through the pipeline

```powershell
'agent.ping', 'agent.version', 'system.uname' | Test-ZbxAgentItem | Select-Object Key, Value
```

-Key binds from the pipeline, one answer per key.

### CommonParameters

This command supports the common parameters: `-Debug`, `-ErrorAction`, `-ErrorVariable`, `-InformationAction`, `-InformationVariable`, `-OutBuffer`, `-OutVariable`, `-PipelineVariable`, `-ProgressAction`, `-Verbose`, `-WarningAction`, `-WarningVariable` (about_CommonParameters).

## INPUTS

- `ZabbixItemKey`: Bound to -Key (ByValue). Represents a Zabbix item key: its text, verbatim, with a parsed view of its name and parameters.

## OUTPUTS

- `ZabbixAgentAnswer`: What a passive agent answered for a key: the value, or that the key is not supported and why.
- `string`: Text.
